why: Inserting the fallback ordering (C_end) made the model more likely to pick punctuation/clause-boundary cuts when those cuts do not split numeral–unit or finite-verb–core attachments; that preserved numeral–unit and similar tight attachments and improved very short bins (≤3/5/7) but at the same time introduced clause-internal cuts that separated verbs from their immediately following complements or moved cuts earlier in longer sentences, producing the negative effects seen in the ≤10/≤99 bins and the small net set of worsened pairs.
lesson: A later revision should keep the numeral–unit/verb–core protections that helped short pieces but ensure the punctuation fallback does not create new finite-verb–complement splits or premature clause-internal cuts that harm longer-span decisions.
